That spread came from one system on a showcase account: Gold Asia Box Weekly Bias, gold, 15 minute bars, 62 trades.

A backtest gives you one path. It is the order the trades happened to arrive in, and that order was luck. Monte Carlo takes the same trades and reshuffles them, so you see the paths you could just as easily have lived through.

The line worth reading is the red one. The unluckiest path finished at -1%. Same edge, same trades, and nothing to show for it. Knowing that before money goes in tells you whether you could actually sit through it.

09.hook: Your systems don't fail one at a time. Sometimes they fail together.
09.ig_caption:
Your systems don't fail one at a time. Sometimes they fail together.

A portfolio test in StrategyDynamics combines your systems into one account over the dates they share. You get the combined equity, the correlation between them, and the losing-together days marked in red: every day two or more systems fell at once.

In this showcase account, six systems ran from May 2026 to November 2026. Together they returned +14.4% with a 5.0% max drawdown and a Sharpe of 2.20. They also had 42 days losing together.

That last number is the one to read first. Each system can look fine on its own and still stack its bad days onto the others. Seeing those days before money is involved tells you whether the book genuinely spreads risk or just repeats it.

Prop firm daily and total loss limits are respected in the test. Portfolio tests are included on every plan, and a tune hunts better settings for the whole book without changing any single system.
